claims.text: Pulumi's component state migrations feature lets component authors ship an upgrade path with the component itself; a migration translates the saved state of a component and its children before Pulumi works out which resources need to change.
Pulumi's component state migrations are new (a recently introduced feature).
The Pulumi component state migrations API is experimental and may change.
A GitHub discussion for feedback on component state migrations exists at github.com/pulumi/pulumi/discussions/24799.
A docs page exists at /docs/iac/guides/building-extending/components/state-migrations/ (component state migrations guide) that covers the callback contract.
The pulumi/examples repository contains an aws-ts-awsx-vpc-state-migration example with v1, v2 and v3 programs and migration code.
A link to /docs/iac/concepts/components/ documents Pulumi components.
A docs page exists at /docs/iac/concepts/resources/options/aliases/ covering aliases.
The pulumi/examples repo has migration files at aws-ts-awsx-vpc-state-migration/v2/migration.ts and v3/migration.ts.
The legacy AWSX VPC component is `awsx.classic.ec2.Vpc`, and it manages the VPC, subnets, route tables, and gateways.
The modern AWSX VPC component is `awsx.ec2.Vpc`.
Replacing a VPC forces replacement of a security group that refers to the VPC's ID, per the AWS CloudFormation EC2 SecurityGroup VpcId property documentation.
If a database is recreated, its replacement does not automatically contain the old data, and deleting the old database without a backup or data migration could mean losing that data.

In the example's v1, the legacy awsx.classic.ec2.Vpc creates a VPC with one isolated subnet, a route table and its association, and an internet gateway, with a security group outside the component that refers to the VPC.
Across all three versions of the example, the AWS resource IDs stay the same and the security group continues to use the same VPC.

The resource trees show v1 with awsx:x:ec2:Vpc containing Subnet and InternetGateway components, v2 with awsx:ec2:Vpc and aws resources as children of the VPC, and v3 with plain aws resources, with the subnet named vpc-isolated-0 in v1 and vpc-isolated-1 in v2/v3.
Pulumi state records both physical resources and components; each record has a Pulumi name called a URN, and managed resources also have a provider-assigned ID such as an AWS VPC ID.

Legacy AWSX wraps the subnet and internet gateway in separate components; modern AWSX removes those wrappers and places managed resources under different parents; the subnet's Pulumi name changes from vpc-isolated-0 to vpc-isolated-1 in the example.

Pulumi aliases handle changes to a resource's name, type, or parent when its saved state remains compatible, but cannot by themselves remove component wrappers and transfer references to replacement resources; a state migration handles that whole change together.
To migrate, a component registers an alias for the legacy component type and a migration callback via the `stateMigrations` resource option.

A state migration callback receives the old component's saved state followed by its children's state, and returns `newState` (the complete set of records replacing the old component and its children) and `successors` (a map from each disappearing old URN to the URN that replaces it).
The example's migration callback is idempotent: if state already uses modern AWSX or plain AWS resources it does nothing, and an unexpected component type raises an error.
The example's `rename` helper copies the saved record and changes its URN, type, and parent while preserving the AWS resource ID and other saved fields.

The Pulumi engine uses the `successors` mappings to update dependencies and resource references elsewhere in the stack, keeping the security group's reference to the VPC valid after migration with the same AWS VPC ID.

In the example's v3, the VPC, subnet, route table, association, and internet gateway are declared directly with `@pulumi/aws`; the second migration removes the AWSX VPC component record, and both the old component and its VPC child map to the new VPC record, which keeps its AWS ID.

Pulumi runs multiple state migration callbacks in order, passing each result to the next; a stack on legacy AWSX can upgrade directly to plain AWS, a stack on modern AWSX skips the first migration, and after both have run the callbacks return no result on later updates.
Keeping earlier migrations with the component lets users skip versions without editing stack state by hand.

After a state migration, Pulumi compares the new program with the migrated state and calls the provider for remaining changes; in this example the preview can still show in-place updates for provider defaults and tags.
Before each upgrade in the example, `pulumi preview` should show no creates, deletes, or replacements for the existing VPC, subnet, route table, association, internet gateway, and security group.
`pulumi preview` evaluates the state migration without saving it, and the update (`pulumi up`) saves the migrated state.

When a component registers a state migration in its implementation, users do not need to write the migration, attach the callback, or edit stack state; Pulumi runs the migration automatically as part of the normal preview and update.
For internal component changes that keep the same inputs and outputs, users can keep their existing component calls without changes.
State migration callbacks (the Pulumi resource option for state migrations) run during previews and updates when prior state exists.
State migration callbacks must be idempotent and must return no result when the state no longer needs migration.
State migration callbacks rewrite resource state without performing provider operations.
A Pulumi component state migration callback is a pure function that transforms the saved state of a component and its children into the state expected by a new component version.
A Pulumi component state migration callback returns the updated state records and successor mappings.
In a Pulumi component state migration result, each successor mapping connects an old URN that is omitted from the result to the URN of the returned resource that takes its place.
If no migration is needed, a Pulumi component state migration callback returns no result.
The Pulumi resource options reference page at /docs/iac/concepts/resources/options/statemigrations/ has a 'callback-api' section that explains the state migration callback API.
The state entries passed to a component state migration callback use the checkpoint resource format documented in the Pulumi developer docs deployment schema (pulumi-resource-state).
Pulumi checkpoint resource state entries include fields such as `urn`, `type`, `id`, `parent`, `provider`, `inputs`, and `outputs`.

A component state migration cannot proceed while resources in the migrated subtree are pending deletion; the unfinished deletion must first be completed by running the migration returning no changes before retrying.
A component state migration cannot proceed when persisted snippet references would need to change; those snippets must be updated or removed first.
A Pulumi component state migration callback that returns no result can remain attached when using update plans or targeted updates.
The Pulumi restrictions on state-changing migration results (with update plans or targeted updates) do not require removing an already-applied migration.
